title: Singularity_studies
summary:
Singularity studies is an academic field where study and research are conducted into the technological singularity, which might be attained by artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and other technologies and sciences. It also involves studying the social implications of such a singularity.

The technological singularity is a hypothetical event in which technological growth accelerates beyond human control, producing unpredictable changes in human civilization. According to the most popular version of the singularity hypothesis, I. J. Good's intelligence explosion model of 1965, an upgradable intelligent agent could eventually enter a positive feedback loop of successive self-improvement cycles, causing an explosive increase in intelligence that culminates in a powerful superintelligence. Ray Kurzweil's 2005 book The Singularity Is Near predicted singularity by 2045.

Singularity studies is still evolving as an academic field, and quite a few challenges remain unresolved in regard to the systematization of theories, research methods, and educational curricula. Interdisciplinary approaches have gained in importance and are drawing much attention in the arenas of scholarly research, intercorporate collaboration, and policy planning. Kento Sasano, a social informatician, AI educator, and inventor, is the president of the Japan Society of Singularity Studies.
